3.speaker: Player
3.text: "Yes, he is a hero for Sordland."

4.speaker: Player
4.text: "I agree, we should abolish this position."

5.speaker: Player
5.text: "Can we reach a two-thirds majority in the Assembly?"

6.speaker: Player
6.text: "No, I think we should respect this law."

7.speaker: Player
7.text: "We could keep the title but take away the immunity clause."

8.speaker: Player
8.text: "So, we only have 3 votes out of 11?"

9.speaker: Player
9.text: "Every President should gain that title after their term."

11.speaker: Lucian Galade
11.text: "If you can get Frens Ricter to work with you on this, our only problem would be uniting our own party. We'll never be able to get NFP to work with us."

12.speaker: Petr Vectern
12.text: "That would be enough to hold him accountable for his actions but why would you want to keep such a title, Mr. President?"

13.speaker: Lucian Galade
13.text: "We need the majority of our 130 seats in the Assembly to vote in favour. With PFJP's full support of 70 votes, we will easily surpass the needed 166."

14.speaker: Petr Vectern
14.text: "The reformists would be completely behind that."

15.speaker: Lucian Galade
15.text: "But it will be tough to unite the USP with all the divisive wings that have formed. You must make them follow you loyally."

16.speaker: Petr Vectern
16.text: "Do you want to protect Tarquin Soll, Mr. President?"

17.speaker: Player
17.text: "We did it before for the elections. We can do it again."

19.speaker: Player
19.text: "Regardless of him, I see no problem with having a special title for great heroes."

20.speaker: Petr Vectern
20.text: "Albin Clavin and his reformist wing would be supporting you. He already weighed in heavily in the committee meetings."

22.speaker: Petr Vectern
22.text: "However, the conservatives would be tough to break. The influence of Soll is still living strong in the party."

23.speaker: Petr Vectern
23.text: "I'm sure it's possible. But regardless of my opinion, we *need* to persuade most of them to support us for passing an amendment to the Constitution."

24.speaker: Player
24.text: "After pushing aggressive changes, I may need the same immunity."

26.speaker: Player
26.text: "It's not unfair that former Presidents get some special treatment."

28.speaker: Petr Vectern
28.text: "We will need to work together to push this agenda."

29.speaker: Player
29.text: "Do you think they can be persuaded?"

30.speaker: Petr Vectern
30.text: "The conservatives have around 40 seats. There are many unaligned people and some of your "loyalists" might decide to show their true faces too."

31.speaker: Lucian Galade
31.text: "We'll need to break the power of the Old Guard within USP first. Most of the conservative wing are still loyal to their Colonel."

32.speaker: Petr Vectern
32.text: "Most of their support is necessary to be able to amend the Constitution. And there is only one person who is key to make them back us."

33.speaker: Petr Vectern
33.text: "And there is only one person who is key to make them back us."

34.speaker: Petr Vectern
34.text: "So we need as many of the conservatives to support us. And there is only one person who is key to make them back us."

35.speaker: Lucian Galade
35.text: "Gloria Tory. She's well respected by the Sollists. She'll be our biggest obstacle in the Assembly."

36.speaker: Petr Vectern
36.text: "But it would be tougher to persuade the judges with this. Mrs. Edmonds may not want to cooperate with you if they believe you're going to get rid of them afterwards."

37.speaker: Lucian Galade
37.text: "And the last one is the question about Soll's legacy. Basically his *Member of Honor* law. It gave him absolute immunity even when he's retired. He is a permanent member of the Assembly as well, but luckily he doesn't really attend anymore."

38.speaker: Lucian Galade
38.text: "I also have reasons to think she might be in Orso's pocket. She will be tough to break, but we'll need her help to get the conservative support."

40.speaker: Lucian Galade
40.text: "According to the Constitution, the Member of Honor not only has legal immunity but the state also covers most of their expenses as well as providing security at all times. It can only be given to someone by an absolute majority vote in the Assembly and the approval of the President."

41.speaker: Lucian Galade
41.text: "If we can reach an agreement with the reformists, we will be very strong in the Assembly to propose such change."

42.speaker: Petr Vectern
42.text: "That's why only Tarquin Soll has that title. He gave it to himself right after his military coup. This law is basically made to save the Colonel and it has a symbolic importance for Sordland because of it."

44.speaker: Petr Vectern
44.text: "We must get rid of this senseless law that protects him. He should be able to face justice for the atrocities that had taken place during his rule."

46.speaker: Player
46.text: "This is already what we wanted to do."

48.speaker: Player
48.text: "Is it possible to pass the Supreme Court?"

49.speaker: Player
49.text: "The Assembly should have oversight over the President."

50.speaker: Lucian Galade
50.text: "That is a better strategy. We'll need to sway some of their members to succeed after all."

52.speaker: Petr Vectern
52.text: "That might be the best thing to do for now. If we agitate the Court further, we might lose our chances with Mrs. Edmonds as well."

54.speaker: Player
54.text: "Not sure if it is correct to chastise the President this much though."

55.speaker: Player
55.text: "And what good does that do to us?"

56.speaker: Lucian Galade
56.text: "They are the biggest obstacle. Even if we pass the Assembly, the Chief Justice will do his best to block our amendments."

61.speaker: Player
61.text: "They should be able to be impeached, why do I get to be impeached but not them?"

62.speaker: Player
62.text: "We should crush the Old Guards to clear ways for further reforms."

63.speaker: Player
63.text: "Maybe we shouldn't make the Supreme Court our enemies just yet."

64.speaker: Petr Vectern
64.text: "This law is particularly dangerous for you in this case. We will be going against the Old Guard, and if we prove to be successful in the Assembly..."

65.speaker: Lucian Galade
65.text: "Most people find the Supreme Court's absolute authority over constitutional changes dangerous. Look at the situation we currently have, Mr. President. The Judiciary has power over every branch."

66.speaker: Lucian Galade
66.text: "We need at least 6 of the 11 judges to vote for the proposal. But Mr. Hawker has enormous influence over the judges."

67.speaker: Petr Vectern
67.text: "Most reformists want the impeachment to be initiated by the Assembly. They think they do not have any power over potential rogue presidents that would abuse their power."

68.speaker: Lucian Galade
68.text: "Well, they need absolute immunity in theory. But look at what reality got us? We've got to deal with the most corrupt Chief Justice in the world, with no chance to deal with him!"

70.speaker: Petr Vectern
70.text: "While I agree that the current court members are *problematic*, this is no way to resolve it. The law is supposed to ensure the judiciary's independence by giving legal protection so they can't be pressured."

71.speaker: Petr Vectern
71.text: "I do not support taking away their power for yourself, Mr. President. The judiciary must be independent and long-lasting."

73.speaker: Petr Vectern
73.text: "We will be ensuring that there won't be another politically motivated Supreme Court."

74.speaker: Lucian Galade
74.text: "It's the question about the immunity of the Judges. While the Anti-Old Guard sentiment is increasing, there are talks that taking away their immunity would give us authority over judiciary."

75.speaker: Lucian Galade
75.text: "Now I'll move unto the 8th Section. We are reaching the end."

76.speaker: Petr Vectern
76.text: "That's why the Old Guard have bargaining chips over us."

77.speaker: Petr Vectern
77.text: "Even Soll knew he had to leave, but we will leave it to the President to decide."

78.speaker: Lucian Galade
78.text: "I have suggested to bring some limitations to decrees regarding their applicability just for arguments sake. While we keep them, we should try to make sure that they will only be used in emergency situations."

79.speaker: Player
79.text: "I will take my time and seriously consider the options before settling on one."

80.speaker: Player
80.text: "Yes, he did. But it took a long time."

82.speaker: Petr Vectern
82.text: "We should reach out to the judges in secret. Some of them might be willing to break rank to support us."

84.speaker: Player
84.text: "I agree. People should be able to elect the same person if they want to."

85.speaker: Lucian Galade
85.text: "We should run-down each of the nine points from the draft, and get your input first. Mrs. Morgna will explain their demands as we go through them."

86.speaker: Player
86.text: "They will surely support a just cause for the country and its future."

87.speaker: Lucian Galade
87.text: "I agree, we could keep that in."

88.speaker: Lucian Galade
88.text: "Hey, if people keep electing one person, that means they really are content. The masses are scared of change."

89.speaker: Player
89.text: "All means are to be considered in order to succeed."

90.speaker: Petr Vectern
90.text: "I agree. We can't allow somebody like Soll holding unto his seat for two decades again."

92.speaker: Petr Vectern
92.text: "We can't allow somebody like Soll holding unto his seat for two decades again. We should establish limits."

93.speaker: Petr Vectern
93.text: "We will make sure the Old Guards won't control the Court any longer, Mr. President."

96.speaker: Lucian Galade
96.text: "We'll go through each of the nine points of the draft, and get your input. Mrs. Morgna will explain their demands as we go through them."

99.speaker: Lucian Galade
99.text: "Yes, they are already trying to hit you since they are aware about the current wind of change. But we aim to cooperate with some of the judges to make sure that doesn't happen."

100.speaker: Player
100.text: "I don't aim to leave any time soon. We keep the unlimited terms."

101.speaker: Lucian Galade
101.text: "Don't forget that the Socialist party and the Worker's Party of Bludia both had close to ten percent vote in the last election."

102.speaker: Player
102.text: "We need the Court to even pass this change. Why would they support this?"

103.speaker: Petr Vectern
103.text: "Yes, we will be collaboratively working on the specifics."

105.speaker: Petr Vectern
105.text: "Yes. This will ensure that there won't be another politically motivated Supreme Court."

106.speaker: Lucian Galade
106.text: "They want us to include previously non-existing term limits."

107.speaker: Lucian Galade
107.text: "According to the Constitution, Nia is a member of the Supreme Court, which means we already have one vote. I am sure she will back us even after what happened, her moral compass is too strong."

108.speaker: Petr Vectern
108.text: "Yes. Tarquin Soll governed for twenty years. It seems his magic is slowly vanishing from the minds of the people, for they believe term limits are necessary."

109.speaker: Lucian Galade
109.text: "We'll start with Section 1. The new Constitution will fix the loopholes regarding the president's absolute veto powers."

110.speaker: Lucian Galade
110.text: "I don't think that's a wise idea to include in the reforms."

111.speaker: Lucian Galade
111.text: "Two of the judges are friends of hers, and of similar opinion about the reforms. Consider them onboard too."

112.speaker: Petr Vectern
112.text: "We could also make it dependent on an enabling act from the Assembly. Sure, it would make the whole process longer but as long as we have a majority, nothing really changes."

113.speaker: Player
113.text: "I don't think presidential decrees need any reforms."

115.speaker: Player
115.text: "We'll work with the reformists to limit the use of decrees."

117.speaker: Player
117.text: "I may need to think a bit longer about this."

118.speaker: Lucian Galade
118.text: "Moving on to Section 3. This is about the impeachment process of the President. Currently, in cases of high treason and breaking the Constitution, the Supreme Court may impeach and try the President."

119.speaker: Petr Vectern
119.text: "Sure. You'll have a long time before we start writing the final proposal together."

120.speaker: Lucian Galade
120.text: "Even though Mr. Ricter put on a whole show about why vetoes should completely be removed, the committee has almost unanimously agreed on fixing the loopholes, thus limiting presidential vetoes."

121.speaker: Petr Vectern
121.text: "Frens will probably demand that we remove them completely. But he forgets that Sordland is a Presidential Republic."

122.speaker: Player
122.text: "We should define a better impeachment process."

123.speaker: Lucian Galade
123.text: "Me neither. I think it's important that the President can act quickly on matters of national importance."

124.speaker: Player
124.text: "I'm sure the rest can be bribed."

125.speaker: Player
125.text: "Who else would be willing to support reforms?"

127.speaker: Player
127.text: "What if we don't succeed? The Court can have me impeached for this."

128.speaker: Player
128.text: "We can't just give away our majority like that."

129.speaker: Player
129.text: "We can't allow communists to enter the Assembly."

130.speaker: Lucian Galade
130.text: "I hope it works out, Mr. President."

131.speaker: Petr Vectern
131.text: "...They will be looking for anything they can declare unconstitutional to tackle you. All they need is the Supreme Court to impeach you."

134.speaker: Lucian Galade
134.text: "I know it is a delicate matter, sir. But you still have time to think about these."

135.speaker: Lucian Galade
135.text: "My suggestion is to add a clause detailing the methods the Assembly may override a veto with some sort of a super-majority. One person should never be able to block the rest."

136.speaker: Lucian Galade
136.text: "Section 6. This is about the presidential decrees. Reformists demand more limitations to the President's executive powers. Mr. Ricter has demanded them to be completely removed."

137.speaker: Player
137.text: "I agree. We should involve the Assembly more in the process."

138.speaker: Petr Vectern
138.text: "There is definitely a demand to involve the Assembly in the process."

139.speaker: Petr Vectern
139.text: "Mr. Ricter and his PFJP definitely wants to see change on this topic. They find our 10% threshold to be antidemocratic. Which is something I disagree with."

141.speaker: Lucian Galade
141.text: "This is regarding the appointment of ministers. Currently, the President is free to appoint anyone from the members of the Assembly. Nobody else is involved with the process."

142.speaker: Lucian Galade
142.text: "The fifth section is about our infamous electoral threshold. Most reformists want to lower the threshold as much as possible."

143.speaker: Narrator
143.text: Lucian continued with the next section.

144.speaker: Petr Vectern
144.text: "Most of them won't. But we already talked about my vote and a possible agreement with Isabel which may change things."

145.speaker: Lucian Galade
145.text: "On to Section 2. The new Constitution will remove the Supreme Court out of the constitutional amendment process."

146.speaker: Lucian Galade
146.text: "We can't just bribe the Old Guards. Judge Garaci and the Chief Justice Hawker will do their best to undermine us."

147.speaker: Lucian Galade
147.text: "I think Judge Edmonds can be persuaded. And in extension, Mr. Dalton and Mr. Martin."

148.speaker: Petr Vectern
148.text: "This is yet another point that was unanimously agreed on by all parties. Tarquin Soll established this rule to protect his '29 Constitution. We all know most of the judges are his sheep."

149.speaker: Lucian Galade
149.text: "You would be opening their way into the parliament in the future if you were to decrease the threshold. It is important that you realize this."

150.speaker: Lucian Galade
150.text: "Three votes, yes. But I believe that Judge Edmonds can be persuaded as well. She and two other judges, Mr. Dalton and Mr. Martin."

151.speaker: Lucian Galade
151.text: "Yes, we have the Socialist party and the Worker's Party of Bludia getting more than five percent vote in the last elections."

152.speaker: Lucian Galade
152.text: "Decreasing the threshold might mean opening their way into the Assembly."

153.speaker: Player
153.text: "They will not be allowed to dictate the negotiations."

154.speaker: Lucian Galade
154.text: "Of course that would also mean that USP might lose its majority in the Assembly, sir."

155.speaker: Player
155.text: "The loopholes give the President too much power."

156.speaker: Player
156.text: "I stand in agreement with Mr. Ricter. The vetoes should be removed."

157.speaker: Player
157.text: "If our own democracy is the reason of our downfall, we will have to accept it."

158.speaker: Lucian Galade
158.text: "They weren't really blinded by the Sollist ideology."

159.speaker: Player
159.text: "Don't worry. With these reforms, we will be even more popular."

161.speaker: Lucian Galade
161.text: "Maybe. But Mr. Ricter doesn't think so."

162.speaker: Petr Vectern
162.text: "If the entire package is to their liking, I don't think Frens will resist his own. He wouldn't say no to such major changes just because of a few small details."

163.speaker: Petr Vectern
163.text: "Yes, but this is a delicate matter. All the party, and I mean, not even Albin wants us to decrease the threshold. They think that... this would destroy our party in the long term."

164.speaker: Lucian Galade
164.text: "Not wrong. The ten percent threshold is what that allowed us to control half of the Assembly with around one third of the majority in the elections."

165.speaker: Lucian Galade
165.text: "But we might try and bribe the centrists of the Court. I think we might get Mr. Dalton and Mr. Martin with a bribe. The toughest will be Mrs. Edmonds."

166.speaker: Player
166.text: "But the high threshold is the reason why Sordish politics has become so isolated."

167.speaker: Petr Vectern
167.text: "I'm sure the reformists would completely support that."

168.speaker: Player
168.text: "We should definitely work to decrease the threshold for better representation."

169.speaker: Lucian Galade
169.text: "Some reformists suggested that the Assembly should nominate the ministers before the President approves them."

170.speaker: Player
170.text: "Do you think it would really hurt the party?"

171.speaker: Lucian Galade
171.text: "Whatever you decide it's important to get a balanced picture. We will be making history by changing the '29 Constitution of Soll."

173.speaker: Petr Vectern
173.text: "This is one of the starting points of the whole discussion about changing the constitution."

174.speaker: Petr Vectern
174.text: "You're right. Even after Soll's resignation, we still have three parties in the Assembly. Even Mr. Kibener's NFP was barely elected."

175.speaker: Petr Vectern
175.text: "Of course, according to the ratio of the party's in government. In our case, it's only us."

176.speaker: Petr Vectern
176.text: "Yes, we'll need to talk to Judge Edmonds. If we can get to her, we might get the 6 votes needed. That's our best bet."

177.speaker: Petr Vectern
177.text: "I agree. Even after Soll's resignation, we still have three parties in the Assembly. Even Mr. Kibener's NFP is barely elected."

178.speaker: Petr Vectern
178.text: "Yes, those three don't seem to be working directly with the Chief Justice Hawker. If we can get to Isabel Edmonds, we might get the 6 votes needed. That's our best bet."

180.speaker: Petr Vectern
180.text: "I don't think this is up to discussion for any reformists."

181.speaker: Petr Vectern
181.text: "Constitutional amendments will still be very difficult to accomplish, particularly because we will keep the two-thirds vote system to be able to propose a change. However, the judiciary will not have the final say in the amendments."

182.speaker: Petr Vectern
182.text: "Mr. Clavin and our party's reformist wing has no problems with the current law. I'm sure PFJP can be persuaded too."
